sentences.en: Back in 2008, I started listening to a podcast called The Memory Palace by my friend Nate DeMeo.
sentences.zh: 早在2008年，我开始收听我朋友内特·德梅奥制作的一档播客，名叫《记忆宫殿》（The Memory Palace）。

sentences.en: It's a history show, and it was unlike anything I'd ever heard before.
sentences.zh: 那是一档历史类节目，和我之前听过的任何节目都不一样。

sentences.en: Each episode wrapped a little-known piece of history inside one of Nate's poetic essays.
sentences.zh: 每一集都将一段鲜为人知的历史包裹在内特富有诗意的散文中。

sentences.en: His stories have an uncanny ability to weave together facts and insight
sentences.zh: 他的故事有一种不可思议的能力，能将事实与洞见交织在一起，

sentences.en: to help us imagine the real lives of historical figures
sentences.zh: 帮助我们想象历史人物的真实生活，

sentences.en: and to call to mind forgotten moments from the paSt.
sentences.zh: 并唤起人们对过去被遗忘瞬间的回忆。

sentences.en: In fact, The Memory Palace is one of the early inspirations for 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 事实上，《记忆宫殿》是《99% Invisible》早期的灵感来源之一。

sentences.en: And now, after 15-plus years of making his podcast,
sentences.zh: 现在，在制作这档播客15年多之后，

sentences.en: Nate has a new book out called, you guessed it, The Memory Palace.
sentences.zh: 内特出了一本新书，书名正如你所猜，就叫《记忆宫殿》。

sentences.en: It's an anthology of some of his best stories from the show, plus a few new ones.
sentences.zh: 这是一部选集，收录了他节目中一些最精彩的故事，还有几篇全新的内容。
